messages:
incident-bot: 🚨 [PROD] high error-rate on serving-runtime — multiple CUDA OOMs, node flaps, and container crashloops observed. Paging @Maya (oncall) for immediate triage. Affected cluster: inference-eu-west-1, service: redwood-serving-runtime. root_ts=1769204322

Maya (oncall): seeing the pager. I'm on it. initial impact: ~12% 5xx across EU region, spikes in tail latency.

Alex: I can help — switching to bridge. what's current autoscaler state?

Nish: autoscaler logs show repeated scale-up then scale-down cycles over the last 6m. policy: busy-window 30s, cooldown 45s. looks like thrash.

Leah: correlation: burst of long-seq requests at 12:10 UTC, then abrupt drop, autoscaler reacted. many nodes started init then failed with CUDA errors.

Samir: grabbing node logs now. snippet from node gpu-7: ```Mar 15 12:11:03 kubelet[1234]: container start failed: runtime: containerd: OCI runtime create failed: failed to start container process: error during container init: could not load CUDA driver: cuInit(0) failed: unknown error```

Maya (oncall): ok, immediate mitigation plan: 1) stop autoscaler (prevent further oscillation) 2) pin min-replicas to current to avoid scale-to-zero 3) cordon suspect nodes and drain survivors 4) fallback traffic to smaller model-variant in us-east temporarily if EU remains unstable.

deploy-bot: accepted runbook step: pause-autoscaler — executing patch to HPA inference-runtime-eu-west-1.

Alex: I'm patching HPA to frozen state: ```kubectl patch hpa inference-runtime -n redwood --type merge -p '{"spec":{"minReplicas":8,"maxReplicas":8}}'``` — setting both to 8 to stop oscillation.

Nish: done. autoscaler scaling events should stop within the next reconcile window.

Leah: cordoning nodes with repeated cuInit failures: gpu-5, gpu-7, gpu-12. draining now (graceful with 60s): ```kubectl cordon gpu-5 && kubectl drain gpu-5 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60```

Samir: note — several pods are in CrashLoopBackOff because the driver init fails on node bring-up after scale. suspect node image or driver mismatch after a recent kernel update we rolled last week. collecting dmesg + nvidia-smi outputs.

Jen (support): customer impact — CS flagged three paying customers seeing 502s for embeddings and chat generation. For now we should send: "We're investigating a regional degradation in EU inference, using mitigations; routing traffic and scaling changes in progress. Asking for patience." Want me to post an interim status page note?

Maya (oncall): yes post an interim. keep message minimal: ETA unknown, mitigation in progress. tag affected customers we saw in logs.

Alex: routing change: temporarily diverting new requests from eu-west to us-east using edge rule. small increase in cross-region latency but reduces error rate for customers. Pushing edge config: ```curl -X POST https://edge-config/api/route -d '{"match":"region==eu-west","action":"proxy:us-east"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer **'```

Leah: edge config applied. traffic shift ~75% successfully offloaded. error rate in EU fell from 12% -> 3% within 90s.

Samir: still seeing some crashloops where pods landed on unpatched nodes. manually redeploying runtime pods with fallback kernel options (disable gpu persistence on init) to avoid driver handshake: ```kubectl rollout restart deployment/inference-runtime -n redwood --field-manager=incident```

Maya (oncall): good. next: gather root cause artifacts: kernel versions, nvidia driver versions, node boot time, autoscaler decision timeline. Nish can you dump autoscaler decision events and HPA history into the incident channel?

Nish: uploading HPA events and scale timeline to the incident jira. quick snippet: ```2026-03-15T12:09:48Z HPA scale to 16; 12:10:21Z HPA scale to 6; 12:11:05Z HPA scale to 14; oscillation period ~36s```

Leah: I captured node boot logs showing kernel 5.19.12 on gpu-7 but driver packages expect 5.18 ABI. mismatch likely introduced during last week's kernel roll.

Samir: that matches cuInit failing — driver unable to bind. If kernel/driver mismatch is root cause, scaling just amplified the blast radius because new nodes got the problematic kernel image.

Maya (oncall): mitigation checklist update: keep HPA pinned, cordon problematic nodes, redeploy pods to healthy nodes, keep traffic routed to us-east until we confirm nodes stable. start rollback of node kernel to 5.18 image on a small pool and validate.

Alex: initiating controlled rollback of node image on a canary pool of 2 nodes. I will not touch prod pool size.

deploy-bot: rollback job queued: node-image-rollback-canary -> running.

Jen (support): posted interim status to status.redwood.ai: "Investigating regional serving errors in EU. Mitigations in progress including routing changes and capacity stabilization. We will update in 30m or when status changes." customers notified.

Maya (oncall): handing off now to Alex — I need to step out for 18m but will keep slack notifications on. Alex, you'll own the bridge and post updates. Samir/Nish handle logs + node rollback. Jen handle customer comms.

Alex: ack — I'm taking over bridge. logging rundown: current state after mitigations: EU errors down to 2.1% 5xx, tail latency improving. rollback job in progress.

Samir: rollback canary nodes completed, validated with nvidia-smi and small smoke tests. canary steady. planning a staggered rollback (2 nodes at a time) to limit churn.

Leah: redeploying remaining pods to stable nodes, adding an extra readiness probe timeout to avoid rapid restarts: ```readinessProbe: httpGet: /health periodSeconds: 10 failureThreshold: 6```

Alex: throttling incoming long-seq requests via token-bucket at edge to reduce chance of another burst: rate=15r/s per org for now.

Maya (oncall): thanks. rough impact summary for post-incident: cause: kernel/driver mismatch introduced during recent node image update; amplifier: aggressive autoscaler cooldowns causing scale thrash; effect: CUDA init failures -> container crashloops -> region brownout and customer 5xx; mitigations: paused autoscaler, pinned replicas, cordoned nodes, routed traffic to fallback region, node image rollback, redeploy with readiness tweaks.

Jen (support): collecting customer tickets and mapping to timeline. will attach examples to the incident jira.

Alex: plan to keep autoscaler pinned for 2 hours after full rollback and validation. then we'll re-enable with more conservative cooldown and bigger target window. Nish will propose tuned HPA settings postmortem.

Nish: will run a simulation on the autoscaler settings against recorded traffic spike and propose changes: increase cooldown to 120s, add stabilization window 3m, set up surge detection to prefer warm standby instead of scale-flip.

Samir: file owners for postmortem: infra (Leah), autoscaler (Nish), runtime (Samir). I'll capture kernel+driver matrices and logs.

Alex: leaving the bridge in 40m to @Maya after validation. still monitoring.

Maya (oncall): thanks all. closing note: if errors reappear, escalate to incident sev2 and page exec team. otherwise we'll convert this to a follow-up postmortem with owners and action items. :+1:

deploy-bot: incident note appended to ticket INC-2026-1743. link: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/INC-2026-1743

Jen (support): scheduled status update to customers in 25m.

Alex: marking incident as "mitigated" in bridge. I'll update when we re-enable autoscaler.

Samir: uploading collected artifacts (node logs, HPA events, kernel diff, crashloop traces) to the incident folder.

Leah: final check — EU error rate stable at 1.8% after 12:37 UTC. continuing watch.

Maya (oncall): back online and rejoining. great work everyone. we'll pick up postmortem tomorrow.
